title: Tire Basics
description: What a tire is made of, the main tire types, and how touring and performance tires differ.
intro: Before you compare brands, it helps to know what you're comparing. These guides explain how a tire is built and how the main types differ, in the tire makers' and regulators' own terms.

title: Reading Your Tire
description: Every marking on the sidewall: size, DOT date code, load index, speed rating, UTQG grades, XL, M+S and max pressure.

title: Tread & Wear
description: Tread depth in 32nds and millimeters, the penny and quarter tests, uneven wear patterns, and how many miles tires last.

title: Pressure & TPMS
description: Finding your PSI on the door placard, checking pressure cold, heat and pressure, the TPMS light, sensors and nitrogen.

title: Damage, Flats & Repair
description: Sidewall bubbles, nails and flats, plug vs patch, pothole and curb impacts, and the spare tire in your trunk.

title: Florida Driving & Weather
description: Rain and hydroplaning, heat and tire aging, hurricane-season prep, Florida tire rules and choosing tires for a no-snow climate.

title: Buying Guides
description: Choosing tires: all-season vs all-weather, all-terrain vs highway, LT vs P-metric and load range, XL vs SL, and run-flat tires.
intro: The letters and symbols on a tire listing decide what it can do and what it can carry. These guides explain them in the tire makers' and regulators' own terms, so you can compare tires on what matters for where you drive. Start from the size, load index and speed rating on your door placard.

title: Wheels & Fitment
description: Wheels and fitment: bolt patterns and PCD, wheel offset and backspacing, staggered setups, and changing tire or wheel size.
intro: A wheel that bolts on isn't always a wheel that fits. These guides cover the numbers that decide fit, from bolt pattern and center bore to offset and staggered sizes, so you know what to check before you order wheels or tires.

title: Maintenance & Service
description: Rotation patterns, balancing vs alignment, a monthly-to-yearly checklist, the week after new tires, and noise or vibration.

title: Tire Age, Storage & Records
description: How old is too old, dry rot and sidewall cracks, storing tires in the heat, recalls and tire registration.

title: Tesla Tires
description: Tires on a Tesla: EV tire basics, factory sizes by model, T-marked and foam-lined tires, rotation and TPMS, flats with no spare, and Florida picks.
intro: Teslas are heavy, quick off the line and quiet inside, and that changes what their tires have to do. These guides stick to what Tesla's owner's manuals and the tire makers publish, so you can check every point yourself.
